Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunited with families in Chernihiv

Humanitarian Evacuation from Oleshky

Hundreds of residents from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have arrived in the Chernihiv region of Ukraine following a rare humanitarian ceasefire. The evacuees, who spent years living under occupation, were transported via a multi-stage journey through Russian-occupied territory, southern Russia, and Belarus before crossing into northern Ukraine on Saturday.

Living Conditions in Oleshky

Residents described dire conditions within the city, which has been under Russian control since February 2022. According to evacuee accounts, the following challenges were reported:

  • Supply Shortages: Civilians reported severe food insecurity, with some resorting to consuming garden vegetation to survive.
  • Security Risks: The population faced constant threats from shelling, drone strikes, and missile attacks.
  • Movement Restrictions: Exit routes were reportedly mined, leading to casualties among those attempting to flee.

The Evacuation Process

  • Logistics: The operation involved a convoy of 25 buses and additional ambulances for those with limited mobility.
  • Timeline: A four-hour window on Friday allowed approximately 750 individuals to depart.
  • Ongoing Need: It is estimated that thousands of residents, including families with children, may still be living in Oleshky and the surrounding areas.

Reunion and Next Steps

The arrival in Chernihiv was marked by emotional reunions between the evacuees and their relatives. Families who had been separated for years met at a processing facility, where many evacuees received medical attention upon arrival. While the immediate danger has subsided for those who successfully left, the displaced families now face the challenge of securing housing and employment to rebuild their lives in safety.

Verification

To verify the details of this humanitarian event, readers can consult official reports from the Ukrainian government’s regional administration in Chernihiv or statements from the International Committee of the Red Cross, which often monitors such humanitarian corridors. As this involves an ongoing conflict, updates are typically cross-referenced with international news agencies monitoring the Belarus-Ukraine border crossings.
